normalized.description: The frontiers for the deployment of 5G cellular networks have grown beyond the limits of the Earth's atmosphere. The 3GPP cellular technologies have become attractive for exploration missions, such as Moon or Mars, as they can provide a standardised scalable, secure, high-capacity, and reliable connectivity. For Moon, the Space Frequency Coordination Group (SFCG) has recently identified several bands for Lunar missions for the deployment of existing Earth communication protocols that includes the cellular element. In parallel to the connectivity, 5G networks can also be used to enhance the performance of navigation services fores een in LunaNet.The communication services will be primarily delivered by satellite-based solutions (already identified in the LunaNet architecture for the Moon). However, although the lunar relay satellites could technically provide surface-to-surface communications for a small number of users, such approach does not scale well as the number of users increases.To serve larger number of users, wireless cellularnetworks on the lunar surface are foreseen. With such deployments, an opportunity to offer 5G space user terminals emerges on the market. A new space-grade 5G user terminal will thus need to be developed, leveraging the technologies from 5G ground terminals, and making them available for exploration missions. This activity will design, manufacture, and test an engineering model of a 5G user terminal in FR1 for exploration missions. To achieve this, the activity willleverage on the current standards, techniques, and technologies. normalized.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a 5G NTN dual active modem prototype with active resource management for improving link reliability and performance, whileoptimizing the space segment resources utilization.TargetedImprovements:-doubling the peak data rate compared to state of art modems.- reduction by half link outage time.Description: The need for a dual-active modem in 5G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) arises from the growing demand for reliable, high-performance communication links particularly inscenarios where terrestrial networks are unavailable or unreliable. A dual-active NTN modem can maintain two simultaneous satellite links, significantly reducing the risk ofoutages caused by shadowing, fading or interference. At the same time, it provides an additional communication channel that enables load balancing across space segmentnodes, helping to distribute traffic efficiently and improve peak user data rates. Active resource management is essential in this context. Strategies must be designed todynamically allocate resources based on real-time link conditions and performance metrics. These strategies should ensure that the satellite system can optimize keyperformance indicators, such as peak data rate and service availability, while minimizing the resources allocated to each link and network node (e.g. payloads). Developingcontrol plane methodologies is also a critical aspect of this solution. The control plane manages the signalling and control information required for the operation of thecommunication links. It enables the system to gather real-time measurements of links conditions, which are essential for making informed decisions about resource allocationand link management. These methodologies also provide mechanisms for communicating decisions to the network including satellites and user terminals ensuring that thesystem can adapt to changing conditions and maintain optimal performance.This activity will develop a prototype dual-active 5G modem, potentially based on open radio stacks, and implement a testbed to evaluate the prototype under realisticconditions. This testbed will include a channel emulator with multiple RF interfaces to emulate themultiple links. Channel performance as well as satellite system resourcesallocation will be tested for various operational scenarios, and both resource management methodologies and control plane techniques will be assessed.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. normalized.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, build, test an integrated D-band transceiver module for high data rate satcom applications.TargetedImprovements: - Enabling D-band satellite links with higher than 10Gbit/sec- Increasing the transmission capacities by a factor of 4.- Smaller footprint and weight than Ka, V-band ISL or even optical ISL.- Less risk for interference as spectrum not completely allocated.- More resilient compared to Optical ISL (e.g. pointing misalignment or thermal effects).Description: The current state of satellite communication technologies, particularly in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations, relies on existing RF and microwave frequencies, which oftenstruggle to meet the growing demand for higher bandwidth and faster data rates. Withthe advent of 5G and the transition towards 6G, current systems face significantchallenges in scaling data throughput and maintaining efficient communication, especially beyond the atmosphere. This challenge is exacerbated by the limitations of traditionalfrequency bands and the complexity of integrating both passive and active elements within semiconductor-based antenna arrays.The introduction of sub-Terahertz frequencies, specifically in the D-Band range of 110 to 170 GHz, can offer a solution to these issues. These higher frequency bands providesignificantly larger bandwidths, allowing for faster data rates, lower power consumption, and smaller,more efficient hardware. However, fully utilizing the D-band spectrumrequires innovative concept to integrate both active components, such as amplifiers and receivers, and passive components, such as filters, with advanced semiconductor-basedantenna arrays.This project will address these challenges by developing two D-Band transceiver module engineering models, using the latest advancements in MMIC (Monolithic MicrowaveIntegrated Circuit) chipset technologies and packaging techniques, enabling future 6G NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) phased-array applications. It will focus on the integrationof both active (e.g. amplifiers, receivers) and passiveelements (e.g. filters) with semiconductor-based antenna arrays. This integration is crucial for power efficiency, reducingpower losses, and ensuring scalable solutions that can be applied across satellite constellations. In addition to addressing integration challenges, the proposed activity willexplore advanced multiplexing techniques, such as Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM), which can significantly increase communication capacity without requiring additionalfrequency bandwidth. This novel approach promises to optimize system performance and unlock greater scalability for satellite communication systems in the 6G era. Theproject will first focus onbreadboarding critical components like the high-power amplifier, receiver, filtering functions and antenna. Subsequently, two engineering modeltransceiver modules with critical functions will be manufactured and tested. A point-to-point link demonstrator will becreated for testing, ensuring that the system meets at leastone specific 6G use case such as Joint Communication and Sensing (JCAS), Multi-orbit Inter-satellite Link (ISL), or Extreme Capacity Backhaul (xHaul).

Building on the existing ESA OSIP co-sponsored Research programme, these positions will be recruited through a dedicated call and alignedwith Explore2040 priorities with a primary focus on science thematics such as local resources, environments  effects, crew health and performance, and habitation and with a secondary focus on enabled science linked to key missions and projects (e.g. ExoMars or ACES).By embedding these PhDs within leading academic institutions, ESA fosters a distributed network of high-potential early-career scientists working on mission-relevant challenges.This strengthens ties with academia, accelerates the maturation of key scientific domains, and ensures a sustained pipeline of expertise closely aligned with Explore2040 objectives.

normalized.description: The overall goal of ARTES 4.0 Business Applications can be summarised as the development of pre-operational services - possibly in partnership - for a wide range of users through the combination of different systems. normalized.title: GSTP ELEMENT 1: DEVELOP: PREPARATION OF ENABLING SPACE TECHNOLOGIES AND BUILDING BLOCKS - STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSAL
normalized.description: The European Space Agency ("the Agency" or "ESA") invites you to submit a Proposal under the General Support Technology Programme, Element 1: "Preparation of enabling space technologies and building blocks''The aim is to prepare and to develop enabling capabilities and the associated building blocks for space related systems and the associated sub-systems. An additional aim is to allow the targeted and coordinated development of the capabilities and building blocks (i.e. among academia and industry) in a given ESA Member State or across different Member States (in a collaborative manner). The intended output is to provide industry with a stronger foundation (i.e. building on this acquired know-how) in order to contribute to new space related system opportunities at national or international levels (institutional, commercial...) The objective is to enable Member States to support the further development of t capabilities and the associated building blocks in their industry. The technology development activities may be prepared in a targeted and coordinated manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed for a targeted type and class of space systems (in terms of performance, cost, size...) and with guiding specifications. The developments are to be performed in a coordinated manner to ensure that industry is able to work on complementary capabilities. The developments may be performed within one Member State or across several Member States in a collaborative manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed to a level such that the industrial entities may then be able to perform developments and eventually produce for concrete/more specific space related developments. The developments may go from a proof-of-concept (via simulation or experiment) up to an engineering qualification model (EQM). They address any technical area (structures, avionics/GNC, power control and distribution...). The spefications are to be linked to the guiding system or sub-system specifications. The maximum amount per activity is 1,000 K. The maximum duration is24 months.

normalized.title: TWELFTH FIXED CALL FOR PROPOSALS UNDER THE PLAN FOR EUROPEAN COOPERATING STATES (PECS) IN BULGARIA
normalized.description: The European Space Agency and the Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation of the Republic of Bulgaria hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above Call for Proposals, which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Bulgarian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types: Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on future ESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 6. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 500,000 (hardware development)/EUR 250,000 (all other activities). Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000.Type E: Phase 0/A/B1 small sat mission definition studies with potential to lead to either a national or a commercial mission, in the area of Earth Observation for Climate, Agriculture, Disaster Management and Environmental Monitoring, enabling the development and demonstration of Bulgarian technologies and products in space. Maximum price for ESA 300.000 Euros. Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRL shall be at least 6 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity. Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in space and answer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000. To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: Type G2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industry and would lead to a new product or service being able to be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon its issue date.
